name: Pangolin Forearm Guards
description: Induces growth of overlapping pangolin-style keratin scales on the outer forearms, from wrist to elbow. The scales are thick, hard, and overlapping — functionally equivalent to natural bracers that protect the forearms from cuts, impacts, and abrasion. The modification is specifically targeted to the forearms rather than full-body coverage, making it cheaper and faster to install while protecting the most commonly raised defensive surface. The scales can be raised and flattened through muscular control — raised, they bristle outward like pinecone armor; flattened, they lie smooth and can be concealed under long sleeves. Crucible Genomics developed the modification as an entry-level defensive package for Shelf residents who can't afford full osteodermal plating.
procedure: Forearm dermal injection with scale growth retroviral carrier, 2 sessions
reversibility: Scale removal leaves textured scarring; regrowth must be gene-suppressed
side_effects: Scales catch on sleeves and tight clothing
Forearm skin underneath scales becomes pale and sensitive from lack of sun exposure
Scale maintenance required — dry, cracked scales are painful
Bristling reflex activates during startle, shredding sleeves
social_perception: Practical and street-credible. Scale bracers signal someone who expects trouble but can't afford — or doesn't want — full body modification. Common among Shelf laborers, couriers, and anyone who blocks with their forearms regularly.
story_hooks: A scale-bracer user's pangolin scales begin incorporating environmental minerals, growing harder and heavier with each shed-and-regrow cycle — their forearms are becoming genuinely armored, but the weight is becoming a problem
A forensic team identifies an attacker by scale fragments left at the scene — pangolin scales shed and regrow like fingernails, and each person's scale keratin has a unique protein signature
